parts.title: Nanotechnology the science of the very small
parts.article:
A Nanoscience and nanotechnology have become very fashionable in recent times. Their prominence has inspired science fiction and raised a lot of hope and hype about the possibilities. But what exactly is nanotechnology? Most definitions agree that it is the manufacture of structures that measure up to 100 nanometres (nm). The diameter of an atom is typically only two or three tenths of a nanometre while that of the human hair is around 1,000,000 nm. Essentially, we are now able to build new structures from atoms and molecules as if we were using the bricks of a children’s construction toy.

B Most of the electronic consumer goods that we use today contain components that measure less than 100 nm. The lasers in our CD and DVD players make use of the properties of semiconductor layers that are just a few atoms in thickness, so we clearly are in the nanotechnology age. There are many other everyday items that we take for granted that have nanoparticles in them. One of these is sunscreen. In the 1990s there were safety issues with many of the sunscreen products available, so scientists at Oxford University set about finding a solution. The product they developed uses nanoparticles of titanium dioxide that are doped with the element manganese. This product is almost transparent to the eye when spread on the skin, and it is effective for much longer than many of the traditional preparations. In this case, we see an example of nanotechnology providing a solution to an existing problem rather than opening up new product areas.

C The technique of using nanotechnology to adapt existing products can also be applied to garments, upholstery, paint, and plastics to improve their longevity. Bearing this in mind, it is interesting to ask whether nanotechnology can help with some of the world’s major current issues. The recent growth in climate change awareness calls a range of things into question. Can we use energy more effectively? Can we reduce the carbon dioxide in the atmosphere? Can we use and purify water more effectively? Can health care be improved? Nanotechnology may very well provide the solutions. There are few times in history when the application of science to improving the human condition has been so apparent.

D We are already making new types of solar cells and batteries by using our newfound ability to manipulate matter at the atomic and molecular scale. If we can capture some of the huge quantities of energy that arrive at the Earth’s surface from the Sun, and store it effectively, we can reduce the need for fossil fuel-based power stations. We are already using nanoparticles and nanoporous materials to capture harmful greenhouse gases, and we may possibly convert some of them back into fuel. There are, however, many technical problems involved, and it will be another decade or so before some of these ideas are deployed.

E Water purification is increasingly challenging and many believe that water, which we take for granted, is going to become more valuable than oil. Currently we do not use water efficiently, and many industrial and food processes leave contamination in water that is potentially toxic and difficult to remove. Nanofiltration may provide the solution to these problems, and may also offer new routes to the desalination of brackish water and groundwater in some parts of the world.

F Food production and processing are becoming more important as the world’s population increases. There are concerns that potentially harmful nano-products might enter the body via the gut. Such concerns are being addressed, but it is even more important to ask questions about how nanotechnology might increase the nutritious yield of food and be adapted to help preserve and package food. There is already evidence to show that it might also be helpful in the primary production of raw food materials, by way of better delivery of pesticides in the field and better extraction of protein and carbohydrates.

G Healthcare is an area where the application of nanotechnology is already exceeding the expectations of ten years ago. It is happening across several fronts: better appreciation of what the ‘natural’ nanoparticles circulating in body fluid do; better methods of delivering drugs to the body via nanoparticles that target the diseased body part; improvements to the diagnostic imaging techniques of ultrasound, magnetic resonance imaging and X-ray computerised tomography. We are now at the threshold of a new subject, ‘theranostics’, whereby nanoparticles will first deliver the diagnostic information to the clinician and then, using the same particle, deliver a form of therapy.

H Nanotechnology is a life-changing technology, making the quality of life better, enabling us to make use of our resources more effectively, thereby protecting our environment, and creating new business opportunities. There are many other examples in the world of ‘new materials’ that also make use of nanotechnology. The possibilities may well be limitless.

Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.
Write your answers in boxes 14–16 on your answer sheet.
Nanotechnology
In the same way that a child may use , scientists are now able to create new structures by combining the smallest particles known to man. We can fully appreciate the microscopic scale of this work by comparing the exact of one atom with that of a single human hair.
A lot of today’s electronic consumer goods, such as lasers, have components that are microscopic in size. They are not the only products relying on nanotechnology. For example, a long-lasting , widely available today, relies on minute nanoparticles for its effectiveness. This was developed in the 1990s as a result of concerns about the safety of existing products.

  • C Further research is needed to turn nanotechnology into practical energy solutions.
  • D Nanotechnology is being used to remove dangerous gases from the atmosphere.
  • E Nanotechnology has helped create cheaper sources of energy.

reference:
Q14

解析 题目空格前是“孩子可能会用到（use）”，对应原文“就像我们在使用儿童拼装玩具里的砖块（bricks）”，因此填bricks。

干扰 你可能想填toy，但题目问的是科学家结合粒子就像孩子使用什么东西来搭建，原文明确说是使用玩具里的“砖块（bricks）”。

句子 Essentially, we are now able to build new structures from atoms and molecules as if we were using the bricks of a children’s construction toy.

Q15

解析 题目问通过比较一个原子和一根人类头发的什么特征能体现微观尺度，原文直接给出了是比较“直径（diameter）”。

干扰 你可能被题目开头的microscopic scale（微观尺度）干扰去原文找相关的抽象词，但这里需要填的是用于精确比较的具体测量维度。

句子 The diameter of an atom is typically only two or three tenths of a nanometre while that of the human hair is around 1,000,000 nm.

Q16

解析 题目问20世纪90年代因为现有产品的安全担忧而开发出的一种效用持久的产品是什么，原文直接点名并花大篇幅解释了这个产品就是“防晒霜（sunscreen）”。

干扰 你可能看到原文后面有nanoparticles或者titanium dioxide（二氧化钛），但防晒霜才是那个进入日常生活的“产品”。

句子 One of these is sunscreen. In the 1990s there were safety issues with many of the sunscreen products available, so scientists at Oxford University set about finding a solution. The product they developed uses nanoparticles of titanium dioxide that are doped with the element manganese. This product is almost transparent to the eye when spread on the skin, and it is effective for much longer than many of the traditional preparations.

Q17

解析 题目要求寻找“对世界上两种重要自然资源的比较”，原文在E段直接拿“水”和“石油（oil）”这两样资源的价值进行了对比。

干扰 你可能会在全篇寻找resources这个词，但雅思阅读通常会把抽象概念具体化，这里就是把“自然资源”替换成了具体的水和油。

句子 Water purification is increasingly challenging and many believe that water, which we take for granted, is going to become more valuable than oil.

Q18

解析 题目要求寻找“纳米技术可能对人类造成危险的提及”，F段明确指出了有害纳米产品通过肠道进入人体的担忧。

干扰 你可能觉得C段提到了很多大问题（气候等），但只有F段切实提到了纳米进入身体内部（肠道）可能带来直接的人身危险。

句子 There are concerns that potentially harmful nano-products might enter the body via the gut.

Q19

解析 题目要求寻找“纳米技术影响了现代作家的主张”，A段提到纳米技术启发了“科幻小说（science fiction）”，就是影响了作家。

干扰 你不要死盯着authors（作者）这个词找，原文是用“科幻小说”这个作品类型来替换指代创作者受到了影响。

句子 A Nanoscience and nanotechnology have become very fashionable in recent times. Their prominence has inspired science fiction and raised a lot of hope and hype about the possibilities.

Q20

解析 题目要求寻找“纳米技术的成就超出了十年前的预期”，G段直接出现了“超越了十年前的预期（exceeding the expectations of ten years ago）”的原词复现与同义替换。

干扰 你可能会被B段的1990s迷惑，但只有G段真正出现了“十年前（a decade ago）”以及“超出预期（more than anticipated）”的完整对应。

句子 Healthcare is an area where the application of nanotechnology is already exceeding the expectations of ten years ago.

Q21

解析 题目要求寻找“纳米技术能带来财务和生态双重好处的建议”，H段并列提到了“保护环境”和“创造新商业机会”。

干扰 你可能只看到了前面段落关于能源和水的生态保护，但只有最后一段把生态（environment）和经济（business opportunities）的好处放在了一起。

句子 Nanotechnology is a life-changing technology, making the quality of life better, enabling us to make use of our resources more effectively, thereby protecting our environment, and creating new business opportunities.

Q22

解析 题目要求寻找“承认还需要更多时间才能实现纳米技术潜力的表述”，D段结尾明确提出这些想法落地还需要“十年左右（another decade or so）”。

干扰 你不要把其他段落探讨的技术难点等同于“需要时间”，只有D段给出了具体的“还要等多久”的时间跨度说明。

句子 There are, however, many technical problems involved, and it will be another decade or so before some of these ideas are deployed.

Q23

解析 题目问关于纳米技术和能源资源作者表达了什么，D段说到虽然有解决能源问题的方向，但存在技术问题且需要十年左右才能部署，这直接对应了C选项的“需要进一步研究以转化为实用的能源解决方案”。

干扰 你可能看到太阳能电池就想选A或B，但原文既没说纳米技术能让太阳能彻底“取代”化石燃料，也没说是“第一次”制造太阳能电池。

句子 There are, however, many technical problems involved, and it will be another decade or so before some of these ideas are deployed.

Q24

解析 D段直接写明了我们已经在利用纳米材料来“捕捉有害的温室气体（capture harmful greenhouse gases）”，完美对应了D选项的移除大气中的危险气体。

干扰 你可能觉得“气体”和“能源资源”关系不大而不敢选，但原文中这句话的后半句直接说到要把这些气体转化回“燃料（fuel）”。

句子 We are already using nanoparticles and nanoporous materials to capture harmful greenhouse gases, and we may possibly convert some of them back into fuel.

Q25

解析 题目问纳米技术如何改善食品生产，F段明确提到它可以用于帮助“保存和包装食物（preserve and package food）”，对应了B选项的让食物保鲜更久。

干扰 你可能会凭借生活常识猜测纳米技术能让作物长得更快（A），但做阅读题必须以原文为准，原文中只字未提生长速度。

句子 Such concerns are being addressed, but it is even more important to ask questions about how nanotechnology might increase the nutritious yield of food and be adapted to help preserve and package food.

Q26

解析 F段最后指出，纳米技术在田间能更好地输送“杀虫剂（pesticides）”，这就对应了D选项的更好地保护食物免受昆虫侵害。

干扰 你不要看到“营养（nutritious）”就过度联想到让食物变美味（C），选项必须能在原文中找到具体的动作支撑，杀虫剂是一个确凿的对应。

句子 There is already evidence to show that it might also be helpful in the primary production of raw food materials, by way of better delivery of pesticides in the field and better extraction of protein and carbohydrates.
